notes: Printed reports are documents now, not photographs of the screen. The reconciliation PDF used to carry everything that was on the screen — the bank picker, the statement-balance box, the Import statement file chooser, the explanatory paragraph, the adjustments editor WITH its input boxes, and the History list with its Open buttons — so a one-page reconciliation came out as a sheaf of pages with the figure you wanted to check somewhere in the middle. RECONCILIATION now prints a Bank Reconciliation Statement: your letterhead, the bank and account number, the statement date, and whether the month is signed off or a draft; then the reconciliation in the order it is read — balance per bank statement, less unpresented cheques, add uncredited lodgements, any adjustments each named, adjusted bank balance, balance per cashbook, difference — followed by the supporting schedules, so the figure being checked is on the first page instead of behind thirty cheques. Ruled Prepared by / Checked by / Approved by lines at the foot. GENERAL LEDGER prints a letterhead, the period and the account, unit or project filters that produced the extract, and now foots its Debit and Credit columns — those totals used to live only in the screen's header strip, which is exactly the part that does not print, so the printed ledger ran off the end without them; if the 2,000-entry cap applied the printed copy says so. EXCEL EXPORTS get column widths, so a long payee no longer arrives as three visible characters, and money reads as 4,575.00 rather than 4575; empty 'uncredited lodgements' and 'adjustments' headings are dropped when there are none. The screens you work on are unchanged, nothing about how figures are calculated has changed, and every other printed document — payment vouchers, payslips, withholding certificates, the GRA schedules, the VAT return, the statements under Reports — already looked this way and is untouched.
